text: {"distance_m": 6, "reasoning_short": "This is a contrast-limited estimate, not a measured result. A 5% contrast needs a contrast sensitivity of about 20. Under indoor lighting, foveal contrast-sensitivity and spot-detection (Blackwell-type) data suggest that a disc at that contrast must subtend roughly 2–2.5 arcmin, larger than the 1 arcmin 20/20 acuity limit. At about 2.3 arcmin (6.7e-4 rad), a 4 mm spot reaches that size at 4 mm / 6.7e-4 ≈ 6 m. The plausible range is about 5–7 m, depending on the assumed threshold angle."}
